cards.text: Jesus has just finished talking to the crowds about John the Baptist (Matthew 11:7-19). Now He turns to the cities where most of His miracles were performed, and He begins to denounce them. Friend, this is NOT a thank-you speech.

cards.question: Jesus denounces the cities that saw most of His miracles. What's the reason?

cards.text: Jesus starts with two towns: "Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida!" Two woes, back to back, like waking up to two missed calls from your boss before 8 a.m.

cards.question: Jesus says if the miracles done in Chorazin and Bethsaida had been done in Tyre and Sidon, two cities outside Israel, what would those cities have done?
Jesus says the day of judgment will be more bearable for Chorazin and Bethsaida than for Tyre and Sidon.

cards.text: Then Jesus turns to Capernaum, the town He went to live in (Matthew 4:13). Talk about getting called out in your OWN neighborhood group chat.

cards.question: Jesus asks Capernaum if it will be lifted up to heaven. No, He says, it will be brought down to ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus brings up Sodom, the city the LORD rained down sulfur and fire on (Genesis 19:24). Friend, when THAT'S the city you're being compared to, the meeting is not going well.

cards.question: If the miracles done in Capernaum had been done in Sodom, what does Jesus say would have happened to Sodom?

answers.text: It would have remained to this day
It would have been destroyed sooner
It would have mocked Him just the same

cards.question: Jesus says the day of judgment will be more bearable for Sodom than for Capernaum.

cards.text: Then the whole tone changes. Jesus declares, "I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth," and He tells the Father why.

cards.question: Jesus praises the Father for hiding these things from the wise and learned. Who does the Father reveal them to?

cards.text: Jesus adds, "Yes, Father, for this was well-pleasing in Your sight." Then He says all things have been entrusted to Him by His Father, and no one knows the Son except the Father.

cards.question: Jesus says the wise and learned can come to know the Father on their own.

cards.text: And now, after all those woes, comes an invitation: "Come to Me, all you who are weary and burdened," Jesus says. Friend, that "all" covers everybody who has ever hit snooze FOUR times and then argued with the alarm.

cards.question: Jesus invites everyone who is weary and burdened to come to Him, and He promises to give them ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, "Take My yoke upon you and learn from Me," and He gives a reason. Friend, I spent years under a pile of old takeout menus in a junk drawer, so I am VERY interested in this reason.

cards.question: Jesus says to learn from Him, because He is ___ and ___ in heart.
Jesus says the ones who take His yoke will find rest for their souls. How does He describe His yoke and His burden?

findings.problem: The question says Tyre and Sidon are 'two cities outside Israel'. That fact isn't in the passage, and it has no reference. Cards 6 and 8 give references for their outside facts (Matthew 4:13, Genesis 19:24), but this card doesn't.

rule.text: References. Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: This card only recites verses 26 and 27. It has no reaction, comparison or storyteller line from Papa Dorin, so it reads stripped down. Card 11, just before it, is also plain, so verses 25 to 27 have no voice at all.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: No card ever tells the baker the key point of 11:27: no one knows the Father except the Son and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him. Card 13 stops at 'no one knows the Son except the Father.' Card 14 only tests the point in reverse, with a statement about the wise and learned. The statement also joins 11:25 to 11:27, which the text never does in words. The baker can finish Prep without ever hearing that the Son reveals the Father.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This two-blank card asks the baker to fill in the exact words of the line, 'gentle and humble in heart,' including their order. No earlier card hints at how Jesus describes Himself. Picking gentle and humble, and in which blank each goes, is about wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning they can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
